Sides are the child's own left and right as read from the UNEPI illustration; please confirm with UNEPI. Vaccine Route Site --- --- --- Polio (OPV), rotavirus, vitamin A Oral Mouth BCG Intradermal Right upper arm Yellow fever Subcutaneous Right upper arm Measles-rubella Subcutaneous Left upper arm Hepatitis B birth dose Intramuscular Left thigh DTP-HepB-Hib (pentavalent) Intramuscular Left thigh IPV Intramuscular Right thigh, 2 cm apart from PCV PCV Intramuscular Right thigh, 2 cm apart from IPV The UNEPI material does not give the route or site for the malaria, HPV or Td vaccines. In FHIR, route and site are recorded on Immunization.route and Immunization.site .

UNEPI's catch-up schedule is summarised as "It is better to vaccinate late than never!" . Dose When to give When not to give --- --- --- Hepatitis B birth dose As soon as possible after birth, ideally within 24 hours and up to 7 days Not after 7 days BCG As soon as possible after birth – 6-week doses: OPV1, PCV1, DTP1, RV1, IPV1 At 6 weeks, or as soon as possible thereafter RV1: not after 2 years of age 10-week doses: OPV2, PCV2, DTP2, RV2 At 10 weeks, or as soon as possible thereafter, and at least 4 weeks after dose 1 Not before 4 weeks have passed since the previous dose. RV2: not after 2 years of age 14-week doses: OPV3, PCV3, DTP3, RV3, IPV2 At 14 weeks, or as soon as possible thereafter, and at least 4 weeks after dose 2 Not before 4 weeks have passed since the previous dose. RV3: not after 2 years of age 9-month doses: MR1, YF At 9 months, or as soon as possible thereafter Not before 9 months of age (except where indicated) MR2 At 18 months, or as soon as possible thereafter, and at least 4 weeks after the previous dose Not before 4 weeks have passed since MR1 General rules: Even if a long time has passed between doses, there is no need to restart the series from the beginning. There is no upper age limit for most vaccines, except rotavirus (under 2 years) and the hepatitis B birth dose (under 7 days). How the logic encodes the catch-up rules For a dose n 1 with scheduled age a n and minimum interval i = 4 weeks, the due date is due( n ) = max( date of birth + a n , date of dose n −1 + i ). A dose is due when its due date is on or before today, upcoming when it is in the future, and expired when today is after its expiration (the last date on which the dose may be given). Expirations: hepatitis B birth dose: date of birth + 7 days; OPV0: date of birth + 1 week (WHO value; Uganda does not state one, see open questions); rotavirus: the day before the 2nd birthday; HPV: the day before the 21st birthday (WHO single-dose age range; Uganda does not state one). The UNEPI catch-up chart lists "IPV1" at both 6 and 14 weeks; this guide reads the 14-week dose as IPV2, consistent with the routine schedule.

The Uganda scheduling logic is the WHO DAK's own scheduling logic, adapted where the Uganda schedule differs. It is built the way the WHO immunization DAK builds it (IG Starter Kit; litlfred/smart-immunizations tools/antigenchecklist.md ): 1. L2, the workbook. input/decision-logic/IMMZ DAK decision-support logic.xlsx is a copy of the WHO DAK workbook. Uganda changes only the cells of the scheduling tables ( IMMZ.D18.S. ) listed below. Each changed row's Comments cell names the Uganda L1 statements it rests on ( library/l1-recommendation-scenarios/uganda/ ). 2. L3, generated. WHO's converter tools/node/processDTSchedule.js turns each adapted table into a PlanDefinition and its Library ( input/fsh/plandefinitions/ , input/fsh/libraries/ ; npm run logic:generate , checked on every pull request). 3. L3, completed. Each adapted CQL library is WHO's finished library of the same name, with only the definitions whose cells changed rewritten, each marked // Uganda: with its L1 key. The new Td table's library is the converter's skeleton, completed from its pseudocode on WHO's DTP data elements. Every other WHO table is used unchanged from the WHO IG this guide depends on. The full record, one row per table with its decision and evidence, is input/l2/dependencies.yaml . no new value sets are introduced. The WHO value set DTP-containing vaccines (IMMZ.Z.DE24) also lists Td (ATC J07AM51). The Uganda logic therefore counts a pentavalent dose only when the vaccine is also in Pertussis-containing vaccines (IMMZ.Z.DE12), and counts a Td dose only when it is not pertussis-containing. This may be worth raising with the WHO guide. Birth doses (hepatitis B, OPV0) are recognised either by the WHO "Dose 0" series marker or by being given before 6 weeks of age, the minimum age of the infant primary series.

This implementation guide is a draft adaptation of the WHO SMART Guidelines Immunization implementation guide to the Uganda routine immunisation schedule of the Uganda National Expanded Programme on Immunisation (UNEPI). It is prepared for review with UNEPI and is not an official publication of the Uganda Ministry of Health. What this guide adds to the WHO guide The WHO guide gives generic, Member-State-adaptable content: data elements, decision logic and scheduling logic for every WHO-recommended vaccine. This guide keeps all of that and adds the Uganda-specific layer: the Uganda routine immunisation schedule and catch-up rules, as published by the Ministry of Health and presented by UNEPI; routes and sites of administration used in Uganda; a line-by-line comparison with the WHO recommendations; computable scheduling logic: the WHO DAK's scheduling tables, adapted cell by cell in a copy of the WHO DAK workbook and converted with WHO's own toolchain, with two WHO parameters configured for Uganda, and test patients in the WHO test format; the UNEPI user requirements for an electronic immunization registry and the service delivery and data flow context; open questions where the Uganda sources are silent or ambiguous and a decision by UNEPI is needed. Sources 1. Uganda Ministry of Health, Uganda Routine Immunisation Schedule (poster), attached to issue 1. 2. UNEPI, User requirements – SMART Guidelines (presentation), attached to issue 1: current immunisation schedule, catch-up schedule, sites of child vaccines, service points, client flow, data flow, current challenges and user requirements for an electronic immunization registry (EIR). 3. WHO, Immunization implementation guide ( smart.who.int.immunizations ), and WHO recommendations for routine immunization – summary tables. Status Draft. Everything marked as an open question needs confirmation by UNEPI before the logic is used for clinical decision support.

Points where the Uganda sources are silent or ambiguous. The draft logic makes the choice shown; each needs confirmation by UNEPI. Question Draft choice --- --- --- 1 Up to what age is the childhood schedule offered as catch-up? ("No upper age limit for most vaccines") The WHO tables as adapted: no upper age except where WHO states one (C15) 2 Hepatitis B birth dose: "up to 7 days" or "under 7 days"? Both wordings appear Up to and including day 7 3 OPV0: is there a cut-off age? WHO IG value: not after 1 week 4 Is there an overdue (defaulter) date for each dose, e.g. for reminders and defaulter tracing? None: a dose is due from its due date until given or expired 5 HPV: upper age limit and whether boys are included Girls only (P10); the WHO single-dose table's overdue date, "Date of birth" + 20 years, kept 6 Td for women of child-bearing age: do earlier tetanus-diphtheria doses (school, previous pregnancies, childhood DTP) count towards Td1–Td5? Td-containing doses that are not pertussis-containing count; infant pentavalent doses do not 7 Td1 "at first contact": should the logic propose Td1 for every woman aged 15–49 seen at any service point? Yes, Td1 is due from the 15th birthday 8 Live vaccines (MR, yellow fever, OPV, rotavirus, BCG): same day or at least 4 weeks apart? Not encoded 9 Doses given too early (before the minimum age or interval): counted, or repeated? Counted 10 Should vitamin A (6, 12, 18, 24 months — the poster lists 6 and 18) and deworming (12 months) be in the scheduling logic? Not encoded 11 Malaria vaccine product (RTS,S or R21), route and site Not stated 12 Rotavirus: if a 2-dose product is used, is the series complete after 2 doses? 3 doses always 13 IPV2: the catch-up chart labels the 14-week dose "IPV1" Read as IPV2 14 Sides of injection sites Read from the illustration (routes and sites) 15 Measles-containing dose before 9 months (outbreak, "except where indicated"): MCV0, not counted towards MR1–MR2? Not counted

Requirements from the UNEPI presentation User requirements – SMART Guidelines . They are recorded here as stated, so they can later be mapped to the WHO guide's functional and non-functional requirements. Programme Vision: a Ugandan population free of vaccine-preventable diseases. Mission: to ensure that every child and high-risk group is fully vaccinated with high-quality and effective vaccines against the target diseases according to recommended strategies. Goal: to contribute to the overall objective of the Health Sector Development Plan in reducing morbidity, mortality and disability due to vaccine-preventable diseases, so that they are no longer of public health importance. Objectives: increase access and demand for immunization services; ensure availability of potent and effective vaccines; build EPI management capacity at all levels; monitor disease trends and programme performance; formulate policy, standards and guidelines. Current challenges (paper-based system) High printing costs; delays in service delivery (time consuming); less accurate data; false zero-dose children (ZDC) and immunization under-coverage (IUC); no flexibility; no real-time processes; vaccine accountability. Expected benefits of digitization Improved data quality; reminders; savings on printing; support for follow-up; identification of real defaulters; improved data use; improved visibility. Functional requirements for an electronic immunization registry (EIR) Id Requirement Detail --- --- --- UG-FR-01 User authentication and access control Username/password, biometric authentication UG-FR-02 Patient record management Personal information, vaccination history and demographic data UG-FR-03 Vaccine inventory management Batch numbers, expiration dates and current stock UG-FR-04 Vaccination scheduling and reminders Scheduling of vaccination appointments and reminders to patients or guardians UG-FR-05 Immunization reporting and analytics Reports such as immunization coverage rates, vaccine wastage and adverse event tracking UG-FR-06 Adverse event reporting Report and document adverse events following immunization (AEFI) UG-FR-07 Integration with health records Integrate with existing electronic health record systems for comprehensive patient health information UG-FR-04 is supported directly by the scheduling logic of this guide. Non-functional requirements Id Requirement Detail --- --- --- UG-NFR-01 Interoperability Data exchange UG-NFR-02 Security and privacy Adhere to data security standards, encrypt sensitive data, secure data transmission UG-NFR-03 Performance and scalability Scalable to accommodate future increases in usage UG-NFR-04 Usability and user experience Easy to use for various users UG-NFR-05 Compliance and regulation Adhere to relevant regulations and standards UG-NFR-06 Training and support Training resources and support to users for effective adoption and usage UG-NFR-07 Reliability and availability Access when needed Other system features Offline mode; parent or guardian portal; multilingual support; vaccine information and education; data migration and legacy system integration; data auditing and logging; mobile application; data quality checks; data sharing permissions; automated reporting to the National Drug Authority (NDA) and the Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI). Proposed EIR architecture Child identification through integration with the birth registration system of the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA / vital registration system), feeding an EIR with a vaccine record module, scheduling and reminders, and data analytics and reporting. Users: health care providers, patients (via app or portal), and district and Ministry of Health staff.

The Uganda routine immunisation schedule, as published by the Ministry of Health and presented by UNEPI. Ages are the scheduled ages; every dose is given at that age or as soon as possible thereafter (see catch-up rules). Children Age Vaccines Diseases prevented --- --- --- Birth BCG, hepatitis B birth dose, OPV0 Tuberculosis, hepatitis B, polio 6 weeks (1.5 months) OPV1, IPV1, DTP-HepB-Hib 1, PCV1, Rotavirus 1 Polio, diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus, hepatitis B, Haemophilus influenzae type b, pneumonia, meningitis, rotavirus diarrhoea 10 weeks (2.5 months) OPV2, DTP-HepB-Hib 2, PCV2, Rotavirus 2 as at 6 weeks 14 weeks (3.5 months) OPV3, IPV2, DTP-HepB-Hib 3, PCV3, Rotavirus 3 as at 6 weeks 6 months Malaria 1, Vitamin A Malaria 7 months Malaria 2 Malaria 8 months Malaria 3 Malaria 9 months Measles-rubella 1 (MR1), Yellow fever Measles, rubella, yellow fever 12 months Vitamin A, deworming – 18 months Measles-rubella 2 (MR2), Malaria 4, Vitamin A Measles, rubella, malaria 24 months Vitamin A – 10 years (girls) HPV, 1 dose Cancer of the cervix Vitamin A (6, 12, 18 and 24 months) and deworming (12 months) appear on the UNEPI schedule but are not vaccines; they are not part of the scheduling logic in this version (see open questions). The UNEPI schedule marks the hepatitis B birth dose, IPV1, the third rotavirus dose, yellow fever and MR2 as newly introduced , and malaria and HPV as yet to be introduced at the time of the presentation. The Ministry of Health poster includes malaria and single-dose HPV in the routine schedule. Women of child-bearing age (15 to 49 years) Dose When Vaccine --- --- --- Td1 At first contact Tetanus-diphtheria Td2 1 month after Td1 Tetanus-diphtheria Td3 6 months after Td2 Tetanus-diphtheria Td4 12 months after Td3 Tetanus-diphtheria Td5 12 months after Td4 Tetanus-diphtheria Diseases targeted UNEPI targets 14 vaccine-preventable diseases: tuberculosis, polio, diphtheria, pertussis (whooping cough), tetanus, hepatitis B, Haemophilus influenzae type b, pneumococcal disease, rotavirus gastroenteritis, measles, rubella, yellow fever, cancer of the cervix (HPV) and malaria. Messages to caregivers (Ministry of Health poster) 1. Ask your health worker for your child's next immunisation date. 2. Keep your child's immunisation card safe and bring it every time you visit the health centre. 3. Report any side effects immediately to the health worker for proper clinical care. 4. Vaccines are safe, effective and free at all government health facilities. Ministry of Health toll-free line: 0800 100 066.

Context from the UNEPI presentation. Service points Static: at the health facility. Outreach: in the community. School. Immunity gap approaches: campaigns, routine, outbreak response (for example COVID-19). Client flow and integrated services at immunization sites Immunization sessions are integrated with family planning, early infant diagnosis, HIV counselling and testing, nutrition assessment, vitamin A and deworming, postnatal care, and management of adverse events following immunization (AEFI). Data flow Micro-plan → vaccination card → immunization child health register (ICHR) → tally sheet → HMIS 105 report → DHIS2 → monitoring chart. Support activities: data cleaning, data quality assessment, data review meetings, and RED/REC categorisation. Current digital systems for immunization System Use --- --- eCHIS Community registries eIDSR Case-based surveillance DHIS2 Routine immunization reporting EPIVAC Campaigns eMR Facility workflows ODK-X Cold chain equipment eLMIS Logistics (approved) Other organisations UNEPI works with: National Drug Authority (NDA), Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI), National Medical Stores (NMS) and the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA).

Test patients follow the WHO DAK's own layout: one directory per Logic library, input/tests/plandefinition/ / .yaml , turned into FHIR test bundles by WHO's tools/node/makeExample.js ( npm run logic:examples ; every file is built on each pull request). Each library's Test Validation expression names, per test patient, the output that should hold, as the WHO libraries do. Library Test patients Checks --- --- --- IMMZD18SHepatitisBBirthDoseLogic UGHepB01, UGHepB02 birth dose due and expiring at 7 days; complete when given on day 3 IMMZD18SPolioBOPVPlusIPVLogic UGPolio01, UGPolio02 IPV 1 due at 6 weeks; IPV 2 due at 14 weeks IMMZD18SDTPOnTimeStartLogic UGDTP01, UGDTP02 DTP 1 at 6 weeks; no booster after the primary series IMMZD18SMeaslesOngoingTransmissionLogic UGMR01 MCV2 due at 18 months IMMZD18SMalariaLogic UGMal01, UGMal02 dose 1 at 6 months; dose 4 at 18 months IMMZD18SHPVSingleDoseLogic UGHPV01, UGHPV02 girls at 10 years; not boys IMMZD18SDTPTdWCBALogic UGTd01–UGTd03 Td 1 at first contact; Td 3 after Td 2; not men The CQL is compiled by the IG build ( fhirbuild.yml , the WHO path). The WHO DAK toolchain has no runner that executes Test Validation on each change; the WHO checklist runs it by hand. That gap is reported to the platform rather than filled with a script in this repository.
